content.text:
I found no claims the record contradicts or fails to support, so I'm submitting every claim as supported with no flags.

Two calls were close, and I counted both as supported:
- **Contributing factor 1, "the existing tests do not cover that case":** Code-Fix (row F1) never says this outright. It follows from F1 adding two new cases that "against the current code … would raise ZeroDivisionError".
- **Contributing factor 3, "any exception … rather than leaving that section out":** F1 only describes the handler in `serve_account_page` as a "broad handler" that turned the ZeroDivisionError into a failed page. The document widens that slightly, but it's attributed to Code-Fix.

Action items and the step that would stop the harm propose rather than claim, so I didn't judge them.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month. The divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month, so the account page request raises ZeroDivisionError. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had not bought anything yet this month, so those pages failed to load.
Account page requests could keep failing with a division by zero for as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on.
Find out why io-shop kept logging monthly-spend-feature=on evaluations after the flag was switched off at {P2.1}
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged account page error rates far above their usual level.
The account page requests failed because building the page raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The service logged this error during {G5309.3} and not before.

Requests reached that code because admin switched feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The service evaluated the flag as off during {G7e5d.4}, partly on in {G971b.6}, and on for every evaluation during {Gce95.4}. The division errors began in the first minute the flag was on for every evaluation.
Shoppers closing their connections, the account page error logged before the onset: it was logged only during {G46bc.3}, while account pages were rendering normally.

Switching the flag on broke the page because, as Code-Fix read the source, the flag sends account pages through a monthly average per item whose divisor is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing yet this month.

No test or check was seen that ran the code path monthly-spend-feature turns on against an account with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing tests do not cover that case.
The flag went from a few evaluations on to every evaluation on in the next minute. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen.
As Code-Fix read the source, a broad handler in serve_account_page turns any exception in the spend summary into a failed account page rather than leaving that section out.
No on-call person was paged when the HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: could have stepped in when the automated revert did not end the errors
The Mitigation Agent judged the revert refuted while io-shop's own flag evaluations still logged monthly-spend-feature=on in {Gce95.5}, after the flag had been switched off.

Argus found an earlier incident in memory, 9c1d4e7a-0000-4000-8000-00000000fee1, where reverting this same flag had been refuted, and tried the same revert again without first finding out why it had not helped then.
The second investigation formed only C2, which blamed the same flag change that had already been tried, so it gave Argus nothing new to try.
